articles.title: 'Kantara’ star Rishab Shetty to team up with ‘Manjummel Boys’ director Chidambaram for two films, first project to be a Kannada sports drama scheduled to go on floors next year - Report
articles.summary: Kannada actor-filmmaker Rishab Shetty is reportedly set to expand his upcoming slate with a two-film collaboration with director Chidambaram, known for
articles.body: Kannada actor-filmmaker Rishab Shetty is reportedly set to expand his upcoming slate with a two-film collaboration with director Chidambaram, known for ‘Jan.E.Man’ and ‘Manjummel Boys’. According to reports, their first project will be a Kannada sports drama, with pre-production already underway and filming expected to begin early next year.Chidambaram and Rishab Shetty reportedly set for two-film collaborationAccording to reports by Telugu360 and Cinema Express, Chidambaram and Rishab Shetty are preparing to collaborate on two projects. Their first film is said to be a Kannada sports drama and will be produced by Shibu Thameens. The project is currently in the pre-production stage, with the makers reportedly planning to commence shooting early next year. Further details about the film, including its cast and storyline, are expected to be revealed at a later stage.Rishab Shetty likely to begin Chidambaram film after ‘Jai Hanuman’Rishab Shetty is expected to take up Chidambaram’s project after completing his current commitment, ‘Jai Hanuman’. The actor is collaborating with ‘HanuMan’ director Prasanth Varma on the mythological epic, in which he plays Lord Hanuman. The film also features ‘Baahubali’ actor Rana Daggubati. Teja Sajja, who played the lead in ‘HanuMan’, is expected to make a special appearance in the sequel. The film follows the story of Lord Hanuman, while continuing the universe established by the first instalment.Rishab Shetty reflects on ‘Kantara Chapter 1’ one year after releaseMeanwhile, Rishab recently looked back at the journey of ‘Kantara Chapter 1’, which completed a year since its theatrical release on October 2. The 2025 film became a major milestone in his career, further expanding the world he had created with the ‘Kantara’ franchise.Reflecting on the making of the film, Rishab spoke about the challenges involved in expanding the story while retaining its connection with its cultural roots, traditions and people. The filmmaker-actor described the process as both challenging and deeply personal.‘Kantara Chapter 1’ box office performance‘Kantara Chapter 1’ went on to become one of the biggest commercial successes of 2025. According to Sacnilk, the film earned over Rs 622.48 crore in India, while its reported worldwide gross stood at Rs 852.36 crore.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Shraddha Kapoor is winning the internet with her latest look from the sets of 'Eetha'. articles.title: Lauren Sánchez's Before-And-After Photos Go Viral As Fans React To Her Transformation
articles.summary: Lauren Sánchez’s changing appearance sparks plastic surgery speculation, with Dr. Gary Linkov discussing procedures she may have undergone over time.
articles.body:
Plastic surgeon Dr. Gary Linkov offers professional observations on potential cosmetic procedures Lauren Sanchez may have undergone based on her changing appearance in before-and-after photos.

Linkov suggests that Sanchez's transformation over the years could potentially include brow lift, cheek implants, buccal fat removal, cheek implant revision, facelift, and lip filler, based on his analysis of her facial features in different age photos.

Online discussions on platforms like Reddit reflect mixed opinions on Sanchez's changing appearance, with some users expressing disappointment in what they perceive as excessive cosmetic alterations and a departure from her natural beauty.

Lauren Sánchez 's before-and-after photos have once again sparked discussion online, with social media users weighing in on how her appearance has changed throughout her years in the public eye.

While the former journalist has not publicly confirmed undergoing the cosmetic procedures being discussed online, plastic surgeon Dr. Gary Linkov has offered his own observations in a YouTube breakdown of her transformation, outlining procedures he believes she may have undergone over the years.

In the video, Linkov compared photos of the 56-year-old at different ages and pointed to several features that, in his opinion, could be consistent with cosmetic enhancements.

Lauren Sánchez's Before-And-After Photos Go Viral

"In her younger years, Lauren has incredible hair density, a strong mid-face and lower-face jaw structure," Linkov said while discussing one of the earliest images.

As he moved through photos of Sánchez at different ages, he suggested there could be signs of a potential brow lift and cheek implants in her 30s. He also noted changes around her jawline and later questioned whether she may have undergone buccal fat removal.

When discussing Sánchez in her 50s, Linkov said her cheeks appeared more prominent and suggested this could potentially indicate a cheek implant revision. He also said he believed there were possible signs of a facelift around this period and later pointed to what he described as potential lip filler.

Importantly, Linkov's comments were his professional observations based on photographs and do not confirm that Sánchez actually underwent any of the procedures he mentioned.

Sánchez's changing appearance has also become a subject of discussion on Reddit , where users shared their own opinions about her transformation.

"Like she really went too far with the face and body alterations," one person wrote.

"Take a look at what she looked like 10+ years ago. It wasn't all that long ago she was absolutely gorgeous," another commenter said.

"She was so naturally pretty before all the surgery," someone else wrote.

Another Reddit user referenced the term "Mar-a-Lago Face," writing, "They call this 'Mar-a-Lago Face'. Super overexaggerated Botox, fill, skin resurfacing with loads of eye makeup. Blonde if you can manage."

The online discussion comes as Sánchez continues to attract attention for her appearance and fashion choices. However, neither Sánchez nor her representatives have confirmed the cosmetic procedures being speculated about by social media users or discussed by Linkov.

articles.summary: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’, starring Tom Holland in the lead, is finally getting its digital release.
articles.body: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’, starring Tom Holland in the lead, is finally getting its digital release. After dominating the box office, the film is now gearing up to take over the OTT space as it is set to become available for digital purchase and rental on October 6, more than two months after its theatrical release.Amid buzz and speculation about the film's release, Sony Pictures confirmed that the film will be available through major digital retailers ahead of its digital release. The film will be available for rentals on Apple TV, Prime Video, Fandango and Sony Pictures Core.‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ set for OTT releaseThe latest instalment in the Spider-Man franchise will be released as a premium video-on-demand (PVOD) title at 12 am ET on October 6.For viewers in the US, the film will be available to buy for USD 29.99 or rent for USD 24.99 through Prime Video and Apple TV. A membership is not required to purchase or rent the film through Prime Video.‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Blu-ray and 4K releaseFor fans who prefer a physical copy of the film, will be able to pre-order it on 4K Ultra HD and Blu-ray. However, they will only be able to get their hands on the copy when it releases on December 15, 2026. The film will include a digital code, allowing buyers to access a digital copy of the film on supported devices. A limited collector’s edition is also available to pre-order.‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to stream on Netflix?There is currently no official Netflix release date for ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’. However, the film is expected to eventually become available on Netflix in the US as part of Sony Pictures’ existing pay-TV streaming arrangement with the platform. The deal includes Sony’s theatrical releases and specifically covers films based on Marvel characters, including the Spider-Man franchise.They also have a broader global agreement under which Netflix is set to become the first subscription streaming home for Sony Pictures films in individual territories as the relevant rights become available.‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to eventually stream on Disney+?There is also a separate agreement between Sony and Disney covering US streaming rights to Sony's theatrical releases from 2022 through 2026 after their initial pay-TV window.As a result, ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ could eventually become available on a Disney-owned streaming platform after its Netflix window.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Aziz Ansari has been doing stand-up for 25 years. He calls his Hypothetical Tour his best yet
articles.summary: The multihyphenate has been touring for nearly 20 months, with breaks for his film projects, and his tour is finally making a stop in L.A. at the Dolby Theat...
articles.body:
Aziz Ansari has been thinking about the fact that he has been on the road for a long time. Long in two ways, he adds.

"I've been doing stand-up for 25 years, although when I say that, it doesn't even sound right," he says by phone from an airport in Australia, where his Hypothetical Tour recently took him. (He will record this as a Netflix special later this month.)

But Ansari, who was preparing to fly to Los Angeles for a show at the Dolby Theatre on Wednesday, has also been feeling the effect of this current tour, which actually started 20 months ago, although it was paused twice — once for publicity for " Good Fortune ," his feature film directorial debut, and once to prepare for another film that didn't end up happening.

At 43, the former "Parks and Recreation" star and "Master of None" co-creator still loves stand-up — more than TV, more than movies — but he finds touring "really exhausting."

"I can't run around the way I used to when I was younger," he says. "I just don't have the same energy. Also, I'm married and it's tough being away from my wife." (The couple lives in London.)

Ansari still gets amped up talking about comedy and was happy to stay on the phone as long as I wanted to … until he said, "Hold on, I lost my boarding pass," and hurried off the phone to sort out next steps. He called back a few minutes later, admitting he'd found it in his pocket. Just another day on the road.

And his current tour is what he prefers to discuss, declining to comment on controversies old and new, like past misconduct allegations (he says he's addressed them in his " Right Now " special) or his more recent stand-up performance in Riyadh and subsequent visit to "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" But the multihyphenate did talk about refining the material in his set, his film work and his appearance on "Saturday Night Live." This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

There's something so pure about stand-up. I'm really grateful for this art form. Movies can be very frustrating — you're waiting on financiers and actors to decide what they want to do — but with stand-up, it's amazing to have an idea and craft it and then to get up and say it to 100 or several thousand people that night and get a reaction.

I'm just grateful people still come out because when you're younger, you take it for granted, and now there are so many comedians out there, so I'm just happy to get to tour. And I'm really proud of this hour, I think it's my best one. I'm just better at what I do and I'm a bit smarter as a comedian.

What kind of material are you talking about on this tour?

I'm married now, which I wasn't on the last tour, and my wife is Danish, and when you get married and are settling in your life, you assess those things in a different way — what does that mean for my culture. In the set, I call myself a "level zero Indian." I just have the look, but I don't know anything about Indian history; I know Gandhi and Mindy Kaling and that's it. And now we're trying to have kids, and I talk about that in the set but also about trying to pass all this stuff down; my parents cook food from our region, and my wife and I won't have that so it's about how I feel about that.

Does it help having fans come out to see your shows now versus having to win audiences over like when you're starting out?

Actually, my goal is to have people that are skeptical and have to win them over. What's challenging is you become famous and you lose a little bit of your radar, so you need a crowd that is a bit less warm because then you get a better sense of how to edit your material. I wish I could find someone like Shane Gillis and switch crowds so I perform for his crowd and we just see how our stuff goes over.

You've been touring with this show for quite a while. Have you changed your material?

I'm constantly moving things in and out. I'll come up with some new bits, but also by the time you have a pretty good hour and are touring with it, you get tired of some of the stuff. I've seen comedians throw out stuff that's really good just because they're tired of it.

It's important to feel present. If you're having a good time and not just plowing through the material, that earns you another 20% with the audience. You end up with a much better show.

As I'm getting ready to record my special, I think about what I'm most excited to put out there because a special is different from a live show. At a live show, people won't leave after 30 minutes, but on Netflix, people will leave five minutes in if you don't grab them.

Now that you've directed "Good Fortune," do you want to make more movies, or do you want to go back to TV?

I do love movies, but I've also had great experiences on TV so I don't know. I do have these movie scripts I want to get done. Trying to have a stand-up career and put together movies at the same time is difficult and somewhat stupid. And you can't really plan your life around movies. TV is much more stable than movies.

For TV, I had conversations about doing a "Master of None" season in Japan where Arnold and I would be there for his bachelor party. But when we did the third season, "Moments in Love" it was so different from the first two — I just took away everything people liked about the show, including myself — and I think I should have just called it a different show. So if I wanted to do the Japan story, it would probably be in a new show.

When people ask if there's going to be another season, I say, "Everything is the show — it's all me observing my life, whether through the show or stand-up or movies. It's all put through this lens of my humor, trying to be shot in an artful way."

Would you ever return to try to complete "Being Mortal," which got shut down during production because of harassment allegations against Bill Murray ?

That movie has so much surrounding it now and it's such a heavy piece, so I want to make something else first, one of the two other scripts I've written, before I even think about it again. But I love the book I adapted it from and I love the story — there's a lot to it.

Your most recent TV appearance was when you played FBI director Kash Patel on "Saturday Night Live." How did that happen?

Someone said there was a lot of stuff on the internet about me playing him, and I thought that would be fun. I'm friendly with Colin Jost so I texted him and said, "I'm in town and if you guys are into it, I would be totally down."

He wrote me back and said he'd talk to Lorne Michaels. And then I didn't hear from him, so I thought they were doing something else. But that Friday, Colin said, "Lorne loves this. Can you be at the studio at 10:30?"

I asked for pages because I wanted to do a good job and he said, "No, we're still working on it." But when I got there, I saw I had quite a bit to do and I got to say, "Live from New York, it's Saturday night." That was a real pinch-me moment.

The next week I asked if we were doing it again and I didn't hear back again until Friday. Over time, I got used to the rhythms of the show. I'd love to do it again. It's a rare dream gig that falls into your lap, and it was such a fun experience.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: In 2015, Sharon Osbourne and late husband Ozzy bought this $11.85 million L.A. mansion, now listed for $16 million after a $1 million price cut
articles.summary: Sharon Osbourne has reduced the asking price of the Los Angeles mansion she shared with her late husband, Ozzy Osbourne.
articles.body: Sharon Osbourne has reduced the asking price of the Los Angeles mansion she shared with her late husband, Ozzy Osbourne. The sprawling Hancock Park estate is now listed for $16 million, following a $1 million price cut from its previous asking price of $17 million.According to the Realtor, the couple purchased the property in 2015 for $11.85 million. They first listed it in 2022 for $18 million and later reduced the price to $17.5 million before taking it off the market. Sharon returned the mansion to the market in April 2026 for $17 million, and it has now received another reduction.The property is being represented by Jonah Wilson and Josh Greer of Carolwood Estates. According to reporting from The Wall Street Journal, Sharon continues to divide her time between Los Angeles and the U.K. and uses an apartment when she is in California.Inside the Osbournes’ Los Angeles mansionThe historic estate spans about 11,565 square feet and is set behind gates surrounded by mature trees and landscaped grounds. The house dates to the late 1920s and was extensively restored during the Osbournes’ ownership.The interiors combine historic architecture with modern luxury. The main level features a grand foyer, living room, formal dining room, wood-panelled library and additional office or staff areas. An elevator connects the home’s different levels.The chef’s kitchen includes modern appliances, white cabinetry and a breakfast area. It opens into the family room and toward an outdoor dining space equipped with a pizza oven and barbecue.One of the home’s standout features is its old-Hollywood-style screening room, complete with red velvet interiors, a fireplace and bar. The room also has signatures from famous visitors, including Elvis Presley, Mel Tormé and Natalie Wood.The upstairs area includes four en suite bedrooms, while the primary suite has two bathrooms and a large walk-in closet. The property has seven bedrooms in total.Outside, the estate includes landscaped gardens, a large lawn and a mosaic-tiled swimming pool. There is also a self-contained guest apartment above the garage.The mansion has also appeared on screen, serving as a backdrop for Sharon & Ozzy Osbourne: Coming Home, which documented the couple’s plans to return to Britain.Why the Osbournes wanted to return to the U.K.Ozzy had spoken for years about wanting to leave the U.S. and return to Britain. In a 2022 interview with The Observer, he expressed his frustration with life in America and cited concerns about gun violence among the reasons he wanted to move back.Health problems delayed those plans. In February 2025, Sharon told Planet Rock that Ozzy would finally return to the U.K. in March and that he was excited to reunite with his Black Sabbath bandmates.That reunion became one of the final major moments of his career.On July 5, 2025, Ozzy performed with Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward at Black Sabbath’s Back to the Beginning concert at Villa Park in Birmingham. It marked the original lineup’s first performance together in 20 years and was billed as Ozzy’s final show.Just over two weeks later, Ozzy died on July 22, 2025, at the age of 76. His death certificate listed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and acute myocardial infarction, with coronary artery disease and Parkinson’s disease with autonomic dysfunction also listed as contributing causes.Sharon’s latest attempt to sell the homeThe $16 million listing marks another attempt by Sharon to part with the California estate following the couple’s long-planned return to Britain.The mansion is significantly more expensive than the $11.85 million the Osbournes paid for it in 2015, but the property has undergone extensive restoration and retains several distinctive features from its Hollywood history.For Sharon, the home is also a reminder of the years she and Ozzy spent building a life in Los Angeles before ultimately returning to the U.K. Now, after Ozzy’s death and another price reduction, the historic Hancock Park estate is once again looking for a new owner.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Brad Pitt: ‘No matter the mistake, you know, you just learn from it,’ a powerful lesson on resilience and the importance of learning from your mistakes
articles.summary: Brad Pitt is a name that needs no introduction.
articles.body: Brad Pitt is a name that needs no introduction. From 'Thelma & Louise' to 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood', he has given us some unique performances; he's played the charming con man, the weary detective, the washed-up stunt double, and the baseball executive who changed how the game was played. He’s been on screens for decades, and his best roles stick with you long after the credits roll. But what makes his perspective worth listening to isn't the fame or the Oscar. It's what he's learned from the harder chapters of his life.Speaking to Entertainment Tonight in 2025, the actor was questioned on the lessons he picked up along the way, and he had the most insightful reply. His words highlighted how mistakes always leave behind a beautiful lesson that ultimately leads to success.Motivational quote of the day by Brad Pitt reads: “No matter the mistake, you know, you just learn from it and move on.”What does the quote by Brad Pitt really mean?He’s saying that instead of getting fixated on past mistakes, it’s better to learn what you did wrong. And move on with your life; if you only analyse your past, you will stop living in the present. The quote works in two parts. The first part is the admission. "No matter the mistake, you just learn from it." He doesn't say some mistakes. He says no matter the mistake. It means every failure carries a lesson. Every wrong turn teaches you something about the road. Pitt has lived through a very public divorce, years of tabloid scrutiny, and personal turmoil that he has spoken about only sparingly. He knows what it feels like to have your mistakes broadcast to the world. He also knows that the only way through is to actually learn from them instead.The second part is the instruction. "Move on. It'll lead to the next success." It's easy to talk about learning from mistakes. It's harder to actually get over them. Pitt's point is that the mistake isn't the end of the story. It's a step. You learn, you adjust, and eventually you get somewhere better.How is the quote by Brad Pitt still relevant today?People are exhausted. Not just tired from work, but tired from everything. The cost of living, the news cycle, the pressure to keep up. There's a constant hum of anxiety underneath daily life, and most people don't have a good way to talk about it. Pitt's quote explains that feeling. He's not saying it will get easier. He's saying you get through it by learning what you can and taking the next step. He’s saying that, in order not to let your past mistakes stop you from future opportunities, you should learn from them and move on.You can either sit in it and let it define you, or you can learn what you can from it and keep moving forward. Pitt has had his failures played out in headlines. But the quote works for anyone who's ever made a mistake and wondered if it was the end of something. It isn't. It's just a step. It'll lead to the next thing if you let it.Early life of Brad PittWilliam Bradley Pitt was born on December 18, 1963, in Shawnee, Oklahoma. His father, William Alvin Pitt, ran a trucking company. His mother, Jane Etta, was a school counselor. The family moved to Springfield, Missouri, when Pitt was young. He grew up in a conservative Christian household. He attended Kickapoo High School, where he was involved in sports, debate, and musicals. He wasn't the kid who dreamed of Hollywood. He was the kid who did everything and did it well.He enrolled at the University of Missouri in 1982, where he majored in journalism with a focus on advertising. He was close to graduating when he decided to leave. He packed up his car and drove to Los Angeles. He had no plan. He had no connections. He had a feeling that he was supposed to be doing something else.He took odd jobs to get by. He worked as a mascot for a restaurant chain, driving around in a chicken costume. He drove limousines. He moved furniture. He took acting classes with Roy London, a teacher who also worked with Sharon Stone and Geena Davis. He started booking small roles. His first credited screen appearance was in 1987 on the sitcom 'Another World'. He played a character named Chris. It was a two-episode role.Brad Pitt's rise to fameHis first significant role came in 1991 with 'Thelma & Louise'. He played J.D., a hitchhiker and small-time criminal who befriends Geena Davis's character. He was on screen for about fourteen minutes. It was enough to make him a star. He followed it with 'A River Runs Through It' (1992) and 'Legends of the Fall' (1994). Both were hits. He was on his way.Then came 'Interview with the Vampire' (1994), 'Se7en' (1995), and 'Twelve Monkeys' (1995). He won a Golden Globe for 'Twelve Monkeys' and received his first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor. 'Fight Club' followed in 1999. It flopped in theaters. Then it became a cult classic. It's now considered one of the defining films of its generation.He founded Plan B Entertainment in 2001. The production company won the Academy Award for Best Picture three times with '12 Years a Slave' (2013), 'Moonlight' (2016), and 'The Departed' (2006). He won his own Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood' in 2020.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Jeffrey Archer: Queen Camilla pays tribute to 'irrepressible' author and former politician
articles.summary: The bestselling author and former politician died on Monday at the age of 86.
articles.body:
Queen Camilla has paid tribute to the bestselling author and former politician Jeffrey Archer, who has died at the age of 86.

"Seldom does an author get to live a life as rich, varied and colourful as any of the characters in their books, or with as many surprising plot twists," the Queen said in a statement.

She added that Archer was "not without flaw", but that "friends will recall him as an irrepressible life force through all the many differing chapters of his life".

The former Conservative MP was jailed for perjury in 2001 after being found guilty of lying and cheating in his 1987 libel case against the Daily Star.

The Queen said he was "an exception to the end" and that it was "with sadness that I learned of his death yesterday, on the eve of publication of his final work and so soon after appearing at my Queen's Reading Room Festival".

Archer was a supporter of the Queen's Reading Room charity.

"My sympathies go to Mary and the family at this time of sorrow. I hope it may be some consolation for them to know what pleasure Jeffrey brought to me and to so many millions of readers through the pages of his works.

"Wherever the next page turns to, I trust there will be champagne and Shepherd's Pie in abundance. Camilla R."

Archer's parties were known for serving champagne and shepherd's pie to guests.

Archer sold more than 300 million books in his five-decade writing career, including the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, and often set the novels in his home town of Wellington, Somerset.

In a statement, Archer's publisher HarperCollins said the author died "suddenly and peacefully at home" on Monday between writing sessions.

Archer was born in north London in 1940 but soon moved to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset and in 1969, Archer was elected MP for the Lincolnshire constituency of Louth.

He served as an MP for five years before becoming Conservative Party deputy chairman.

He moved to the House of Lords in 1992 but was jailed for four years for perjury and perverting the course of justice in 2001.

He was found to have lied in libel action he had brought against the Daily Star newspaper, in which he was awarded £500,000 in damages.

The Star had alleged Archer had slept with a sex worker.

The peer was found by the court to have perverted the course of justice by asking a former friend to give him a false alibi and producing fake diary entries to back up his story.

He was also found to have perjured himself on oath during the libel trial.

He was released from jail in 2003 and returned to the House of Lords until he retired in 2024.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described Archer's death as "devastating news".

"We will miss him very much," she told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday, adding that he had texted her earlier on Monday.

Badenoch said he was "very much loved by the Conservative family", adding: "I'm glad that I saw him recently."

Speaking about what she described as "other parts of his life", she said: "He did serve his time, he made amends, and he wanted to do a lot of good in the world."

Former Conservative prime minister Sir John Major said "we have lost a man who lived one of the most remarkable lives of our age", and that he will be "much missed – and long remembered".

Archer's last novel, Adam and Eve, was released on Tuesday.

Broadcaster Gyles Brandreth told BBC Breakfast that he was with Archer on Sunday. "I mean, literally 72 hours ago, doing a show in the West End of London celebrating this book, the publication, and he was in great form.

"He didn't really acknowledge that he'd changed much since being in prison, but I think he became a nicer person in some ways, a gentler, a milder person after the prison experience."

Former Conservative Party leader Iain Duncan Smith described Archer as "a remarkable man who did everything at full bore", adding: "There were simply no half measures with him."

Other former ministers also paid tribute. Sajid Javid said Archer had been a "dear friend", while Sir Jeremy Hunt said Archer had "showed enormous kindness with his advice about how to become a writer".

James Cleverly said the author and politician had been "a huge personality and fantastic storyteller", and that he had been very supportive when his wife Suzie was recovering from cancer.

Reform UK member and former Conservative minister Nadim Zahawi, wrote: "Jeffrey Archer was a dear friend and an extraordinary human being. His gift for storytelling was matched by his wit, warmth and boundless energy. Life was never dull in Jeffrey's company."

Author and former politician Jeffrey Archer dies aged 86

Jeffrey Archer: bestselling novelist whose political career ended in scandal

Archer 'nostalgic' about Somerset before death

Last week, Archer returned to his former school to promote his last book.

"It's wonderful to come back. What I got a real thrill about when I was walking towards the library is seeing the young boys and girls and thinking, 'that's the next generation'," Archer said at Wellington School.

Archer had been due to attend the Cheltenham Literature Festival on Saturday to discuss his final novel.

He and his wife Mary had celebrated their 60th wedding anniversary this year, HarperCollins said.

The couple have two sons and five grandchildren.

articles.title: Halle Berry seeks return to 50/50 custody of son Maceo with Olivier Martinez, calls herself domestic violence victim amid abuse claims, asks court for tie-breaking authority
articles.summary: Oscar-winning actress Halle Berry has asked a Los Angeles court to reinstate the 50/50 custody arrangement she previously shared with her ex-husband,
articles.body: Oscar-winning actress Halle Berry has asked a Los Angeles court to reinstate the 50/50 custody arrangement she previously shared with her ex-husband, actor Olivier Martinez, for their 13-year-old son, Maceo, amid an increasingly bitter legal battle over their child.Berry, 60, made the request in a series of legal filings submitted Monday, days after Martinez was granted a temporary domestic violence restraining order against her following allegations that she had physically abused their son during an incident on September 26. Berry has strongly denied the allegations and maintains that she has never physically, emotionally or otherwise abused Maceo.According to court documents reviewed by the Daily Mail, Berry has asked the Los Angeles Superior Court to restore the custody arrangement she and Martinez had in 2023. She is also seeking to be given tie-breaking authority on important decisions involving their son and wants Martinez to comply with court-ordered therapy sessions.Halle Berry denies allegations of abusing son MaceoIn an ex parte application filed Monday, Berry directly addressed the allegations against her and characterized herself as a victim of domestic violence.“I have never physically, emotionally, or otherwise abused Maceo,” Berry said in the filing. “I am a victim of domestic violence, and I help victims of domestic violence. I am not a perpetrator of violence. I would never hurt our child.”Berry's latest court filing comes as her custody dispute with Martinez escalates. The former couple, who were married from 2013 to 2016, have previously been involved in legal disagreements over the care and upbringing of their son.Martinez, 60, recently sought legal protection following the September 26 incident, alleging that Berry had been physically abusive toward Maceo. The actress has denied those claims.Halle Berry accuses Olivier Martinez of making unilateral decisionsIn her latest filing, Berry outlined several concerns regarding what she described as Martinez's conduct in their co-parenting relationship.She alleged that Martinez has continued to make “unilateral” decisions concerning Maceo's education and extracurricular activities without informing her or obtaining her consent.Berry also claimed that Martinez has repeatedly placed their son in the middle of disagreements between the former couple. According to her filing, she believes their ongoing conflict has affected Maceo's behavior and their relationship.The actress claimed that Maceo would sometimes return from visits with his father appearing angry and combative. She said he would talk back to her, behave untruthfully and engage in what she described as “sneaky” behavior.Berry further alleged that it could take two to three days for Maceo to readjust after returning home from Martinez's care, claiming that a similar pattern would repeat when he went back to his father.Halle raises concerns over Maceo's education and mental health supportA significant part of Berry's filing focuses on what she describes as disagreements over Maceo's educational and therapeutic needs.She claimed Martinez has refused to take necessary steps to secure educational and psychoeducational services for their son. Berry also alleged that Maceo's soccer activities have been used as leverage during disagreements over his educational and therapeutic needs.According to Berry, Martinez has portrayed her as a risk to their son by allegedly communicating what she described as false stories to Maceo's teachers and therapists.Berry argued that Martinez's alleged lack of cooperation regarding their son's psychological and educational needs has been detrimental to his overall welfare.She further claimed that delays in obtaining early intervention had allowed Maceo to fall further behind in school, worsened his acting-out behavior and caused additional strain in her relationship with him.Halle Berry says Maceo should not make major decisions himselfBerry also addressed Martinez's alleged view that their son is old enough to make certain decisions for himself.According to the actress, Martinez has told her that Maceo should be allowed to make his own decisions in order to keep him happy and improve his relationship with his mother.Berry said she remains attentive to her son's thoughts and feelings and encourages open communication with him. However, she argued that a child should not be responsible for making major decisions concerning education, healthcare, extracurricular activities and general welfare.The actress has therefore asked the court to restore a structure in which both parents have equal authority, while giving her the final say when they cannot reach an agreement.Halle Berry brings fiance Van Hunt into custody disputeBerry's relationship with musician Van Hunt has also emerged as an issue in her latest legal filing.The actress claimed that Martinez has refused to accept Hunt's presence in their family and said her fiancé plays an important role in Maceo's life.Berry alleged that Martinez's lack of acceptance of Hunt has prevented Maceo from participating in family therapy involving Berry and Hunt. She argued that such therapy could help establish a healthier environment for their son as part of their blended family.The issue is another point of contention between the former spouses as they disagree over how Maceo should be supported emotionally and therapeutically.Olivier Martinez asks court to reject Halle Berry's requestsMartinez has pushed back against Berry's latest filing and asked the court to reject the requests she has made.In a responsive declaration, Martinez cited the temporary restraining order he obtained after alleging that Berry had physically abused their son. He also claimed that Berry had not followed the appropriate protocols when submitting her requests and suggested that the filings were intended, at least in part, to influence the public narrative surrounding their custody dispute.Neither side has backed down from its respective position, with Berry denying that she poses any danger to Maceo and Martinez maintaining his allegations.Custody battle intensifies between former coupleBerry and Martinez have been involved in a complicated custody dispute for years, with disagreements reportedly extending to education, therapy, extracurricular activities and parenting decisions.Their latest legal battle comes at a particularly contentious moment, with the temporary restraining order and competing custody requests placing their son's welfare at the center of the court proceedings.A source previously cited by Daily Mail described the relationship between the former couple as extremely strained, claiming there is significant animosity between them.As Berry seeks to restore the 50/50 custody arrangement and greater decision-making authority, Martinez is asking the court to maintain the restrictions arising from his recent allegations. Berry has denied the allegations against her, and the competing claims remain part of the ongoing legal proceedings.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: HBO Max and Paramount Plus will merge into a single streamer under Skydance
articles.summary: Paramount Plus and HBO Max will merge into a single service following Paramount’s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.
articles.body: HBO Max and Paramount Plus will become one streaming service under Paramount’s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. In a press release announcing the completion of the deal, Skydance — the name of the combined companies — says both streamers will “unify into a single service over time.” Skydance CEO David Ellison hinted at this possibility in March, saying during a call with investors that merging Paramount Plus and HBO Max would give the combined companies “a little over 200 million direct-to-consumer subscribers.” There are still no details about the timing of this change, or the name of the merged streamers, which HBO CEO Casey Bloys will oversee. Merging the two streamers could help them compete with Netflix, which last reported having 325 million subscribers in January. The move will put top shows from both services onto a single platform, including titles like Mobland, Yellowstone, The White Lotus, and House of the Dragon.

articles.title: Apple TV’s great year continues with Small Prophets
articles.summary: Apple TV continues to add great new series to its streaming service, this time with the charming supernatural comedy Small Prophets.
articles.body: Apple TV has had a really great run in 2026 — and a cozy new addition is helping expand its lineup even more. As the streaming service has attempted to grow in order to better compete with the likes of Disney and Netflix, it has steadily broadened the range of its series. This year has included everything from a pair of OnlyFans dramedies to the horror-comedy hybrid Widow’s Bay, alongside the return of some big names like Ted Lasso and Silo. And now you can add Small Prophets to the growing list of new flavors on Apple TV. The six-episode comedy actually premiered on the BBC earlier this year, but it’s going to be streaming on Apple TV on October 7th. It’s a smart, silly, sweet, and occasionally stressful show, and also one tinged with just a bit of the supernatural. Sort of like British humor meets magical realism. The show centers on Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley), who has been living like something of a hermit since his girlfriend Clea disappeared without a trace seven years ago. He’s essentially put his life on hold waiting for her to return: He works a job he hates at a hardware store, helps take care of his elderly father (Michael Palin), and lives in a house still stuffed with old boxes full of Clea’s things. Then one day his dad has an idea: He tells Michael a secret, alchemical recipe that will let him grow tiny magical beings that can answer any question. And since Michael is desperate to know the answer to one particular question — will he ever see Clea again? — he decides to try it, despite not really believing it will work. What follows is chaotically comical. Michael ends up partnering with his curious coworker Kacey (Lauren Patel) to grow the creatures, called homunculi, but at the same time his previously simple life becomes much more complex. Michael’s father keeps getting into trouble at his nursing home, his neighbors keep threatening to call the council because of his messy yard, and Clea’s broke brother Roy (Paul Kaye) is trying to claim the house so he can sell it and get out of debt. All the while, the homunculi are growing in both size and power. [Media: The best word to describe Small Prophets is charming. Much of this comes down to Michael himself. While he seems like an isolated shut-in on the surface, with his big beard and aloof personality, he’s actually incredibly funny and even lovable… at least to the people he likes. He’s constantly cracking jokes and helping out his small group of family and friends. To everyone else he’s a bit of an asshole, but in a weirdly funny way, like how he constantly shushes his boss so he can take personal calls at work. At one point he impersonates Santa Claus to get out of a mugging. And there’s a bittersweet note to his always-on humor, as Michael does all of this while holding onto the unlikely possibility that Clea is still out there. It’s a low-key show, but one that is also extremely strong in basically every regard, with an excellent supporting cast, just the right amount of mystery, and the perfect mix of sweet and silly tones. The goofy and heartwarming nature of Small Prophets also makes it a particularly good fit for Apple TV, since there’s nothing else quite like it on the service. It slots nicely between Ted Lasso, which is comforting in a much more overbearing way, and Widow’s Bay, which similarly mixes comedy with the supernatural, but with an end goal of horror. Small Prophets, on the other hand, is much more whimsical; even the homunculi themselves look more like stop-motion puppets than anything scary. For a long time the major complaint about Apple TV was that it simply didn’t have enough shows. Once you were done with the big names, like Severance or Slow Horses, there wasn’t a whole lot else to watch. But slowly and steadily that has changed, and 2026 has marked something of a turning point for the streaming service. Part of this comes down to a large number of returning shows, from Sugar to Dark Matter, that have further built out the library. But a lot of it has to do with new shows like Small Prophets that are able to fill in those gaps while also broadening the scope of what’s available on Apple TV. The good news is that this trend looks to continue, at least for the foreseeable future. The next few months of Apple TV include a serial killer thriller (Nocturne), a heist drama (12 12 12), and one of the service’s most ambitious sci-fi shows to date (Neuromancer). And as for Small Prophets? It ends with a promising “to be continued.”

articles.title: Quote of the day by John Cena: ‘As long as you’re physically capable, there’s always a goal you can strive for,’ a powerful life lesson that reminds everyone to keep looking ahead
articles.summary: Discover John Cena's powerful quote on setting new goals and staying motivated after achieving great milestones in life. Learn how Cena's journey emphasizes the importance of continuous growth and challenge.
articles.body: It feels good when you finally get something you’ve spent so much time working for. But once you get there, it can also leave you thinking about what you want to take on next. That has been the case for John Cena, who has often moved from one challenge to another instead of simply stopping at one achievement.Over the years, Cena has taken on plenty of different roles. He became a major name in WWE and later stepped into movies, television and other areas of entertainment. Each new chapter gave him something different to work toward. His approach is simple: reaching a goal does not mean you have to stop.Today’s quote of the day by John Cena reads, “As long as you’re physically capable, there’s always a goal you can strive for.”What does the quote by John Cena mean?Cena’s words are about what happens after you finally get something you have wanted for a long time. You might feel proud of reaching that goal, but it does not mean you suddenly run out of things to work toward.He explained this while looking back at his first WWE Championship win. At the time, Cena thought becoming champion would be the biggest moment of his career. But once he had the title, his thinking changed. He wanted to keep it, defend it and eventually win it again.In a retrospective interview with WWE, Cena said, “I truly thought that would be it…but it's weird, because this thing just never ends. As a kid, you want to be WWE Champion. Then, you're WWE Champion. And then, it's not enough. You want to keep it. So OK, let's win it again. That's what I love about this: As long as you're physically capable, there's always a goal you can strive for.”That is what makes the quote interesting. Cena is not saying that people should spend every minute chasing success. He is talking about having something that keeps you interested, motivated and willing to push yourself.Why does John Cena’s message still matter today?It is easy to think that one big achievement will make you feel completely satisfied. Maybe it is getting the job you wanted, graduating, getting a promotion or finally reaching a personal target you have worked toward for years. But once you get there, you may find yourself asking the same question Cena describes: what comes next?Looking at it this way, having another goal is not always about putting more pressure on yourself. Reaching one goal can simply open the door to something else. And the next goal does not have to be something huge. It could be picking up a new skill, getting better at something you already like or finally giving something unfamiliar a try.That way of thinking has been a part of Cena’s career for years. Even after reaching some of the biggest milestones in wrestling, he continued looking for another challenge.Early life of John CenaJohn Cena was born on April 23, 1977, in West Newbury, Massachusetts. Sports became an important part of his life while he was growing up, and he later attended Springfield College, where he played football.After college, Cena moved to California and started working toward a career in bodybuilding. His plans eventually changed when he became interested in professional wrestling and began training for the sport.That decision would eventually take him to WWE and set him on a completely different career path.How did John Cena rise to fame?Cena stepped into WWE for the first time in 2002, facing Kurt Angle on SmackDown. He didn’t win that night, but the match marked the start of what would become a much bigger chapter in his career. At the time, there was no way of knowing how big his career in WWE would become.As he spent more time in WWE, Cena started figuring out what kind of performer he wanted to be. His “Doctor of Thuganomics” character gave him a completely different edge, especially with his raps and outspoken personality. Fans began taking notice, and before long, Cena was becoming one of the wrestlers people wanted to see.His popularity soon took him to Hollywood, with roles in films such as ‘The Marine’, ‘Trainwreck’, ‘Bumblebee’, ‘The Suicide Squad’, ‘Fast X’ and ‘Barbie’. He also starred in ‘Peacemaker’ and hosted the series ‘WWE Evil’, expanding his career beyond wrestling.In 2005, Cena reached a milestone he had been working toward when he defeated JBL at WrestleMania 21 to win his first WWE Championship. It was a huge moment, but it did not make him feel as though he had done everything he wanted to do.Instead, winning the title gave him something else to think about. He wanted to keep it, defend it and eventually win it again. In many ways, that is exactly what his quote is about: being proud of what you have achieved while still having another goal in mind.Over the years, his career moved beyond wrestling too. He took on acting roles, appeared on television and became familiar to audiences who may never have watched WWE.Looking back at his career, the meaning behind his quote becomes easier to understand. One achievement gave Cena something to celebrate, but it also gave him another reason to keep going.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Robert Kelker-Kelly, ‘Days of Our Lives’ and ‘General Hospital’ soap opera star, dies at 62
articles.summary: Soap opera star Robert Kelker-Kelly has died, according to a Missouri medical examiner’s office.
articles.body: Soap opera star Robert Kelker-Kelly has died, according to a Missouri medical examiner’s office. He was 62. A spokesperson for the Missouri Office of the Regional Medical Examiner, which serves Franklin, Jefferson, and St. Charles counties, confirmed in a statement to NBC News that Kelker-Kelly died on Saturday. The medical examiner’s office did not list the cause of death, and said that its “normal timeline for death certification is approximately 12 weeks,” according to the spokesperson. The office did not have any additional information to share at this time, the spokesperson said. Kelker-Kelly was best known for playing Bo Brady on “Days of Our Lives” from 1992 to 1995 and Stavros Cassadine on “General Hospital” from 2001 to 2014. “Days of Our Lives” addressed his death in an Instagram post on Monday. “Rest in peace,” the post reads. Kelker-Kelly got his start in daytime television when he joined the cast of “Another World” as Sam Fowler in 1987. He then joined “Days of Our Lives” in 1992, where he starred alongside some of the soap opera’s most notable stars, including former “Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” cast member Lisa Rinna. Rinna and Kelker-Kelly played each other’s love interests on the show. The actor and reality star described having a tumultuous relationship with Kelker-Kelly behind the scenes in her recently published memoir, “You Better Believe I’m Gonna Talk About It: A Candid New York Times Bestselling Memoir of Hollywood, Aging, and Owning It All.” “We hated each other,” Rinna wrote, adding that Kelker-Kelly “made my life a living hell on the set of ‘Days.’” Rinna and Kelker-Kelly won a Soap Opera Digest Award in 1995 for the hottest soap couple. The year prior, Kelker-Kelly won one of the awards for outstanding lead actor. Kelker-Kelly was born in Wichita, Kansas, according to IMBD. He married fellow “Days of Our Lives” star Miriam Parrish in 1997 before the pair divorced in 2013.

While talking to PEOPLE at the Gala, Rod weighed in on how he was born around eight years after the franchise first started and “cognizant of about 35 of them." However, he is extremely proud of his father’s legacy and the life that he imbued in ‘Star Trek.'He further commented on the legacy of the space war series, adding, “I have embraced [Star Trek] for the last 35 years. And of course, I’ve learned that Star Trek is not just science fiction—it really talks about a future where we no longer fear the differences between us,” he tells PEOPLE at the event. “In fact, we realise that diversity is something that we can learn from and grow from and become better.”Rod Roddenberry talks about how ‘Star Trek’ is ready for new storiesFurther in the interview, Roddenberry opened up about how the franchise, which has been going since his father created the first concepts in the 60s, is ready for something new and fresh. He continued, “I think Star Trek is ready for new stories. Going back to the well, in my opinion, and bringing [previous cast] or characters ... We’ve done that. Let’s start on a new adventure. We’re certainly entering a unique time right now with technology and all sorts of things, and to explore that more in a respectful, careful, but optimistic way would probably not be too bad of an idea. But it also has to be a good story too. So I’m not sure what that looks like yet.”Roddenberry has carried on his father’s legacy while working as an executive producer for ‘Star Trek: Discovery,' ‘Star Trek: Picard,' ‘Star Trek: Lower Decks,' ‘Star Trek: Prodigy,' ‘Star Trek: Strange New Worlds,' ‘Star Trek: Khan,' and ‘Star Trek: Starfleet Academy.’Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Fox Nation reveals how Rudy Giuliani broke the Mafia's grip on New York
articles.summary: Fox Nation chronicles how Rudy Giuliani used the RICO Act to indict heads of the infamous Five Families in the 1985 Mafia Commission Trial that changed organized crime forever.
articles.body: Before he was "America's Mayor," Rudy Giuliani was a U.S. attorney on the hunt for some of the nation's most notorious Mafia leaders. The newest season of the hit Fox Nation series is peeling back the curtain behind those brave efforts to bring some of the most dangerous men of the 20th century to justice. During the third season of 'Stories of the American Mafia,' narrated by Eric Shawn, the episode "Rudy and the RICO Act" chronicles Giuliani's rise from little-known lawyer to prosecuting some of the country's most feared crime bosses. The show reveals how during the 1980s, soaring crime rates in Manhattan created a perfect breeding ground for the Mafia to tighten their grip on the city. "When you have a vacuum like that, you're gonna have this shadow government step in," former NYPD inspector Paul Mauro explained in a new episode. But Giuliani had a plan to fight back against the rising tide of organized crime syndicates. TRUMP PICKS JAMES MCDONALD TO LEAD POWERFUL SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF NEW YORK AFTER JAY CLAYTON'S DEPARTURE The former NYC mayor established the Mafia Commission Trial in 1985 and indicted 11 people, including the heads of the infamous 'Five Families.' The indictments were made using the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), using charges such as murder for hire, extortion, and labor racketeering. In short, New York City prosecutors could target entire Mafia organizations rather than specific individuals, making it easier to hold criminals accountable. "Previously, you had to make these cases based essentially on conspiracies," Mauro said. "What RICO did is change that paradigm. All you had to do is to have agreed to act on behalf of an organization, and then having done something on behalf of that organization. And what it meant was that guys would flip." FORMER GAMBINO ASSOCIATE TURNED NEW JERSEY COUNCILMAN ACCUSED OF RUNNING LOANSHARKING RING WHILE IN OFFICE Former Gambino associate Louis Ferrante described Giuliani's prosecution strategy as cutting "the head off the Hydra," praising his top-down efforts to take down the Mafia groups. "That's not going to be able to repair itself," he said. "Not because they couldn't replace the bosses, but they couldn't replace the boss with the talent that they once had. And that's what led to the beginning of the end for the Mafia. And realistically, I would argue that they've never recovered from that." SAMMY 'THE BULL' REVEALS WHY HIS LOVE FOR JOHN GOTTI TURNED INTO PRISON HATE In other riveting episodes of "Stories of the American Mafia" Season 3, viewers can witness the short rise and fall of Murder, Inc., the brutal murder of William "Billy Batts" Bentvena, FBI agent Joe Pistone's undercover takedown of the Bonanno crime family, and more shocking true stories of the American Mafia. Former FBI undercover operative Giovanni Rocco joins Mauro and Ferrante throughout the season, adding in-depth analysis to these stunning but true mob stories. articles.title: From Ellen DeGeneres to Adele: 6 highly expensive celebrity home listings
articles.summary: Explore the extravagant homes of celebrities like Ellen DeGeneres, Adele, and more, featuring unique amenities and stunning price tags.
articles.body: For some celebrities, a home is much more than a place to live. Celebrities may spend much of their lives in the spotlight, but their homes are often designed as a place to escape it. Some of these properties include huge pools, private gyms, theatres, and acres of land. When they eventually go up for sale, however, the multimillion-dollar price tag often gets people talking.Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi — $96 millionEllen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi made headlines in 2024 after selling their sprawling Carpinteria, California, estate for $96 million.Their Carpinteria property stretched across about 10 acres and included an 8,000-square-foot home, a cabana and a guest cottage. The estate also had an enviable setting, sitting on a bluff overlooking the Pacific.The Wall Street Journal reported that DeGeneres and de Rossi paid roughly $70 million for the property less than two years before selling it. The quick turnaround made the deal particularly notable.Robbie Williams — More than $70 millionRobbie Williams' former Beverly Hills estate had one detail that sounds almost unbelievable: 27 toilets.The British singer mentioned the number during a 2020 BBC Radio 1 interview. The huge property was about 20,000 square feet and came with 10 bedrooms, an 11-car garage, a wine cellar, a tennis court and an orchard.The unusual home eventually went to another music superstar. According to the Los Angeles Times, Drake agreed to pay more than $70 million for the estate in 2022.Adam Levine — $60 millionAdam Levine and Behati Prinsloo's Montecito property had already lived a celebrity life before the Maroon 5 singer owned it. The estate was originally built for actor Rob Lowe.The couple bought the approximately 3.4-acre property for $52 million and later renovated it. Among its features were a tennis court, koi pond and even a chicken coop.In 2025, the couple sold the estate for $60 million, with TMZ reporting the transaction. The sale added another impressive figure to the celebrity-heavy Montecito property market.Sylvester Stallone — $58 millionSylvester Stallone's Beverly Park mansion eventually became the home of another global entertainment star: Adele.The singer paid $58 million for the property in 2022, according to the Los Angeles Times. Stallone's former home covered around 21,000 square feet and included a movie theatre, gym, swimming pool and several other luxury spaces.One detail from the sale became especially memorable. Adele reportedly wanted Stallone's Rocky Balboa statue to stay at the property, allowing a small piece of the actor's most famous character to remain behind.Mark Wahlberg — $55 millionMark Wahlberg's Beverly Park mansion was the kind of property where the list of amenities almost sounds excessive.The actor's roughly 30,500-square-foot home sat on 6.2 acres and featured a movie theatre, wine cellar, gym, skate park, grotto-style pool and a five-hole golf course.There was also a basketball court designed around Wahlberg's love for the Boston Celtics. After initially asking $87.5 million, the actor eventually sold the estate for $55 million in 2023, the Los Angeles Times reported.Ryan Seacrest — $51 millionRyan Seacrest's Beverly Hills estate had another celebrity connection even before it left his hands. The television personality had purchased the property from Ellen DeGeneres for $36.5 million in 2012.Nearly a decade later, Seacrest sold the compound for $51 million in 2022, after originally putting it on the market for $85 million.The nearly three-acre property included a 9,200-square-foot main house, two guesthouses, a pool house, gym, swimming pool and underground garage. The Los Angeles Times reported that Seacrest still made a profit on the sale, although the final figure was considerably below his original asking price.What makes celebrity homes so fascinating?The price is only part of the story. These properties often come with famous previous owners, unusual features and years of Hollywood history attached to them.A home can change hands, but its celebrity connections can remain. Stallone's mansion became Adele's, DeGeneres' former estate later belonged to Seacrest, and Robbie Williams' enormous Beverly Hills property eventually attracted Drake. articles.summary: ‘Harf’ at Lucknow Museum explored Mir Taqi Mir’s life and poetry, highlighting his Lucknow years, major works, and lasting influence ahead of Koshala Lit Fest.
articles.body: tnnLucknow: Poetry and real-life incidents from the life of 18th-century Urdu poet Mir Taqi Mir came alive at Lucknow Museum Heritage and Art on Tuesday. Titled ‘Harf’, it was presented by Koshala Literature Festival and LMHA.Founder of Microlit, Ajay Jain, and storyteller, author and dastango Himanshu Bajpai Lakhnavi brought together perspectives from cultural heritage, literature and oral storytelling. articles.title: In 2013, Dionne Warwick filed for bankruptcy as tax debt crossed $10 million;  nearly $7 million was owed to the IRS
articles.summary: Dionne Warwick had the kind of music career that seemed almost impossible to slow down.
articles.body: Dionne Warwick had the kind of music career that seemed almost impossible to slow down. The voice behind ‘Walk On By’, ‘I Say a Little Prayer’ and ‘Do You Know the Way to San Jose’ had already become a Grammy-winning star and an international name. But by 2013, Warwick was dealing with a problem that had little to do with music.On March 21, 2013, the singer filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey. Her own bankruptcy petition listed just $25,500 in assets against more than $10.7 million in liabilities. Associated Press reported that Warwick's Chapter 7 filing included nearly $7 million owed to the IRS for 1991–1999 and more than $3 million in California business taxes. Most of that liability was connected to taxes.Dionne Warwick's tax debt had built up over decadesThe bankruptcy documents give a more complicated picture than simply saying Dionne Warwick “owed $10 million in taxes.” The filing showed nearly $7 million owed to the Internal Revenue Service for tax years 1991 through 1999. She also listed more than $3 million in California business taxes.So while some of the tax debt went back to 1991, it would be misleading to say that the entire $10.7 million had been sitting unpaid since then. The liabilities had accumulated across different tax obligations. Warwick's representative, Kevin Sasaki, blamed the situation on what he described as “negligent and gross financial mismanagement” during the late 1980s and 1990s.According to a statement given by Sasaki at the time, Warwick had tried several times to arrange repayment plans with the IRS and the California Franchise Tax Board. He said those attempts were unsuccessful and that interest and penalties continued to grow. The statement also said Warwick had paid the actual back taxes, while the penalties and interest continued to accumulate.Dionne Warwick was still earning money when she filed for bankruptcyAnother detail in the bankruptcy filing makes the story even more striking. Dionne Warwick reported monthly income of around $20,950. Her monthly expenses were almost exactly the same, at approximately $20,940.In other words, there was barely any room left each month. The filing showed just how difficult it was for Warwick to deal with the accumulated liabilities even while she was still earning money from her career.She was 72 years old when she filed for bankruptcy and had spent decades performing and recording music. Her career had included hit records, Grammy Awards and work with some of the biggest names in popular music. Yet the financial problems had followed her for years.Why did Dionne Warwick file for bankruptcy?For Dionne Warwick, bankruptcy was ultimately a way of dealing with debts that had become too large to manage normally.The Chapter 7 filing brought her financial situation into the open, including the gap between her assets and what she owed. The court documents showed that her total assets were only about $25,500, compared with liabilities exceeding $10.7 million.That contrast is probably the part that made the story so startling. This was not a singer who had suddenly stopped working. Warwick was still earning an income. She still had a career. But years of tax problems, interest and penalties had created a financial burden that was much bigger than what she could realistically handle.Dionne Warwick's bankruptcy was about more than one unpaid tax billThe Dionne Warwick bankruptcy story is often reduced to one number: $10 million. But the court filing shows why that number needs some context.The IRS portion covered tax years from 1991 through 1999, while the California liabilities involved business taxes. Her representative also argued that financial mismanagement and the accumulation of interest and penalties had made the situation worse over time.That makes the story less about a celebrity suddenly losing all her money and more about what can happen when financial problems are left unresolved for years. Warwick's music career, meanwhile, was far from over.The bankruptcy became one difficult chapter in a career that had already lasted for decades. For someone whose songs had become part of the soundtrack of several generations, the idea of Dionne Warwick facing bankruptcy was hard to reconcile with the image of the glamorous, successful singer audiences had known for years. But the numbers in her March 21, 2013 filing told their own story.Behind the famous voice and the long list of hit songs was a financial problem that had been building quietly for years — until there was no easy way around it.Disclaimer: This report is a journalistic account of a recent court development. articles.title: Freddie Jackson, R&B star who sang ‘You Are My Lady,’ dies at 70
articles.summary: Freddie Jackson, whose smooth vocals swept an entire generation off its feet, died Monday night, his family announced on Instagram.
articles.body: Freddie Jackson, whose smooth vocals swept an entire generation off its feet, died Monday night, his family announced on Instagram. He was 70. “Freddie was more than a legendary voice. He was a kind, generous soul who loved his fans, his family, his friends, and his music with everything he had,” his family wrote. “For decades he gave us the songs that became the soundtrack to our love stories, our celebrations, and our most treasured memories,” the post went on. “That gift will live on forever.” His hit 1985 single “You Are My Lady” became one of the most recognizable songs at weddings, engagements and any time a romantic mood needed to be set. “To everyone who ever sang along, danced, or felt something when Freddie took the stage: thank you. You were family to him, and he carried your love with him always,” his family said on social media. No cause of death was given. In 2024 the singer announced that he had been diagnosed with kidney disease and planned to partner with the National Kidney Foundation to spread awareness. Jackson said that after much thought and reflection he was finally able to speak publicly about his deeply personal journey. “This journey has been challenging, but I am not facing it alone,” he said. “My close friends, my manager and music family, and all of you are here with me keeping me going.” The foundation said it was deeply saddened to learn of his death, and praised him for his courage during the darkest of times. “His battle with kidney disease touched many lives, and his courage will not be forgotten,” the foundation said in a social media statement. One in seven Americans have chronic kidney disease, which can lead to weak bones and heart disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control. Nine out of 10 people don’t know they are afflicted with it. Jackson was born in Harlem and first learned to sing gospel music before graduating to more adult themes. His silky voice earned him two Grammy nominations and a slate of platinum and gold records, Rolling Stone reported. In 1989, the New York Times wrote that he was “one of black pop’s most elegant performers, a singer who can turn a heartbreak ballad into a world view.” ‘’My music is for people who like to hold hands in concert,’’ he told the Times. “If people could diminish some of their hate, the chaos and trouble in life wouldn’t be so strong,” he added. “At my shows, I see people who don’t know each other end up talking to each other.’’

articles.title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion privacy fence approved despite neighbors’ concerns over Lake Erie views, landscaping and shared sewer line; 1,190-ft fence planned around 3.5-acre property
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's efforts to increase privacy at their newly purchased lakefront mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, have cleared a key local hurdle.
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's efforts to increase privacy at their newly purchased lakefront mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, have cleared a key local hurdle. The village's Architectural Review Board unanimously approved a new privacy fence for the couple's property, although the proposal came after discussions with neighbors over Lake Erie views, landscaping, deer and a shared sewer line.According to Cleveland.com, the board voted on September 8 to approve the fence along Lake Shore Boulevard, subject to several conditions. The design and appearance must match a fence on Ingall Brook Lane, the gates must follow the same design, and the fence's height must align with the property's existing stone walls.The decision comes as the couple continues work on the exterior of the $5.35 million property they purchased earlier this year. Cleveland 19 News previously reported that the planned exterior changes include a taller fence, landscaping and privacy planting measures.Fence plan was revised after neighbors raised concernsThe proposal considered by the board was different from the property's original plan. Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction told the board that the initial proposal called for an eight-foot fence that would extend farther toward Lake Erie.Following discussions with neighbors, the plan was revised to a six-foot fence, with a corridor left open to preserve views of the lake.“We agree you need to be able to see the lake,” Kutz said. “That’s why you live in Bratenahl. It’s beautiful.”The proposed fence will be approximately 1,190 feet long and positioned two feet inside the property's boundary. It will also include two gates to provide access to manholes connected to a shared sewer line.Patrick Hyland, the property's house manager, told the board that representatives for the property had also paid $7,500 to repair a damaged section of the sewer and had the line cleaned.Neighbors divided over privacy and lake viewsThe fence proposal prompted a range of concerns from residents of the affluent Lake Erie community.Katherine Bolton, who said her family has lived in Bratenahl for 35 years, raised concerns about landscaping planned near the shared sewer line. She expressed concern that tree roots could eventually damage the line and potentially create problems for future property owners.Another neighbor, Chuck Bauernschmidt, objected to anything that could obstruct views of Lake Erie. He also questioned the proposed spear-shaped top of the fence, arguing that deer could become caught on the pointed posts. He suggested a flat-top design instead.Victoria Broer, who lives next to Bolton, questioned whether moving the fence closer to the property line would provide a significant security advantage and said she preferred keeping it farther back.The concerns reflect the broader tension surrounding the property's renovation plans, with some residents emphasizing privacy while others want to preserve the area's established lake views. Cleveland 19 News reported that community members had also raised concerns about lost views, the timing of notifications and the impact of the proposed exterior changes.Landscaping plan will face separate reviewWhile the Architectural Review Board approved the fence, it did not approve the landscaping proposal at the same time.Board chair Judith McGlinchy said landscaping would have to be submitted separately and reviewed through the appropriate village departments.“The landscaping plan should be a separate submission and done through planning commission and the building department in terms of following what’s required for a landscape plan,” McGlinchy said.Cleveland 19 News reported that the landscaping plan was scheduled for a separate review and would require additional documentation, including a licensed survey showing the new sewer line, property boundaries and existing tree sizes and species.Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio mansionSwift and Kelce purchased the Bratenahl estate for $5.35 million. The 3.5-acre lakefront property sits along Lake Shore Boulevard overlooking Lake Erie and is a short drive from Cleveland.The purchase has added another Northeast Ohio connection for Kelce, who was born in Westlake and grew up in Cleveland Heights. The property became part of the couple's Ohio ties after the NFL star and Swift married in New York City on July 3.The couple's decision to enhance privacy at the estate has attracted considerable local attention. While some residents have welcomed the high-profile neighbors, others have focused on ensuring that renovations do not substantially alter the character of the neighborhood or interfere with established lake views.For now, the fence has received the village board's approval, while the landscaping proposal remains a separate matter before Bratenahl officials.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body:
Serie A side Udinese pulled off a coup when they signed former Real Madrid man David Alaba on a free transfer about a week ago. This came right after Oumar Solet was excluded from action due to injury and the decision to sign the Austrian did catch the eye for many.

The defender was presented to the media as a Udinese player today and he was asked a host of questions about the decision.

articles.title: Sebastian Maniscalco’s SiriusXM channel is hurting up-and-coming talent, comics say
articles.summary: Comedians are calling on Sebastian Maniscalco to restore up-and-coming talent to his SiriusXM channel. The channel replaced Raw Comedy, which featured stand-up shows from a wider range of comics.
articles.body: Comedian Sebastian Maniscalco is facing backlash from fellow comics who claim his takeover of SiriusXM’s Raw Comedy channel is harming up-and-coming talent, as reported earlier by Deadline. Many established comics, including Patton Oswalt and Margaret Cho, have posted videos online calling on Maniscalco to carry on Raw Comedy’s legacy by highlighting newer comedians on his channel, instead of mostly focusing on well-known ones. SiriusXM launched Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio in April, which is “curated and headlined by Sebastian himself,” according to the satellite radio provider. The move replaced SiriusXM’s long-running Raw Comedy channel featuring uncensored stand-up comedy shows from a range of talent. Now, the channel airs Maniscalco’s own show, alongside a stream of stand-up content that comedian Dan Soder says features “very famous comics who are dead or who don’t necessarily need the money.” The widespread criticism comes as Stand Up for Standup, a nonprofit organization that provides resources for comedians in need, published a report about the channel’s shift away from emerging talent, who rely not only on the visibility they receive from appearing on the station, but also on the royalties they earn from SiriusXM. The organization says that since March, the spins on Maniscalco’s channels have decreased from a wider net of more than 800 comics to a much narrower pool of 275 artists, largely skewed toward celebrities. “We believe this shift, both in the overall quantity of artists enjoying plays on Channel 102, and the change in distribution across all spin-getters favoring the top few, is bad for comedians, and bad for the future of comedy,” Stand Up for Standup says. [Media: “There’s a lot of up-and-coming comedians who are depending on the money and the checks that they get from Sirius,” Oswalt says in an Instagram video. “But 500 of them have been booted off of Sirius… You can easily reverse this decision. Get those young comedians back on the Sirius channel. Let them get those checks.” Many other comedians, including Liz Miele, Kyle Kinane, and Michelle Wolf, have called out Maniscalco as well. In a statement to Deadline, SiriusXM says Maniscalco’s channel “introduced a new creative direction and a regularly evolving programming mix for the channel,” adding that “SiriusXM continues to invest in comedians more than any other audio platform.” Neither SiriusXM nor representatives for Maniscalco immediately responded to The Verge’s request for comment.

articles.title: Michael Douglas admits he almost left his wife for his 'Basic Instinct' co-star after affair
articles.summary: Michael Douglas reveals in his memoir "One Helluva Ride" that he had affairs with his "Basic Instint" co-star and Kathleen Turner on set of hit films.
articles.body: Michael Douglas is letting go of all his secrets in his new memoir.
