While many at the time believed Douglas and his on-screen love interest, Sharon Stone, were having an affair in real life, the actor admitted in the memoir that it was actually actress Jeanne Tripplehorn with whom he was having the affair. articles.title: Eva Marie Saint, star of ‘On the Waterfront’ and ‘North by Northwest,’ dies at 102
articles.summary: She was one of the last surviving luminaries of the Golden Age of Hollywood.
articles.body: Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar- and Emmy-winning star best known for playing a New Jersey dockworker’s grieving sister in the Elia Kazan drama “On the Waterfront” and an elegant government agent in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller “North by Northwest,” died Tuesday. She was 102. Saint’s death was confirmed by her representative, Jeff Sanderson, who attributed it to natural causes and said she was “surrounded by family and loved ones.” Saint was one of the last surviving luminaries of the Golden Age of Hollywood, revered by generations of cinephiles for the understated complexity of her most celebrated performances. In a career that started in the early 1950s and spanned more than seven decades, Saint appeared in 20 feature films. She was a prolific television performer, collecting five Emmy nominations and winning one for the 1990 miniseries “People Like Us.” Saint collaborated with some of the most fabled performers and filmmakers of the classical era. She co-starred with Marlon Brando, Cary Grant, Paul Newman, Gregory Peck and Elizabeth Taylor in movies from giants like Hitchcock, Kazan, Vincente Minnelli and Otto Preminger. The entertainment industry changed dramatically during Saint’s life, but she persevered through each new chapter with a smile and a sense of humor, even appearing as Clark Kent’s adoptive mother in “Superman Returns,” released in 2006. “You know how to stay young? Go with the flow,” Saint told Turner Classic Movies (TCM) in 2014. Eva Marie Saint was born July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey. She started acting while she was a student at Bowling Green State University, graduating in 1946. She then launched her career as a radio actor in New York City and took classes at the city’s famed Actors Studio. In the late 1940s and early 1950s, Saint appeared on small-screen programs such as “Actors Studio” and “The Prudential Family Playhouse.” She was applauded for her turn in a 1953 televised version of Horton Foote’s “The Trip to Bountiful,” starring Lillian Gish, an icon of silent cinema. Gish proved to be one of the key mentors in Saint’s young life. In an interview with TCM, Saint recalled what Gish would say to younger actors fretting about their future: “It’s today and tomorrow, and don’t get cranky.” In 1951, Saint married Jeffrey Hayden, who went on to become a prolific television director and producer. (He died in 2016 at age 90.) Saint’s big-screen breakout came when she was cast in Kazan’s “On the Waterfront,” now considered one of the landmarks of midcentury American drama. She played Edie Doyle, the sister of a slain Hoboken dockworker and the conflicted love interest of washed-up prizefighter Terry Malloy (“I could’ve been a contender!”), played by Marlon Brando. Brando, as she later recalled, seemed at once “really adorable” and somewhat intimidating during the production of “Waterfront.” He was possessed of such an intense acting talent, she told TCM, that “I felt that he could see right through me.” Saint’s feature film debut earned her an Academy Award for best supporting actress at the ceremony in 1955, two days before she gave birth to her first child. Frank Sinatra called out her name, and the visibly pregnant Saint took the stage to deliver a brief acceptance speech. “I may have the baby right here,” she said with a laugh. “But I would love to thank Elia Kazan and Sam Spiegel, Marlon Brando, Karl Malden, Boris Kaufman, all the longshoremen. Thank you.” The same year she won an Oscar, Saint was nominated for an Emmy for her work in the TV version of Paddy Chayefsky’s play “The Middle of the Night.” The following year she received another Emmy nod for her turn in a TV musical production of Thornton Wilder’s “Our Town.” Saint’s film career flourished, too. She co-starred with Bob Hope in “That Certain Feeling,” picked up a Golden Globe nod for her role in Fred Zinnemann’s addiction drama “A Hatful of Rain” and appeared alongside Montgomery Clift in Edward Dmytryk’s “Raintree County.” But then came arguably the best-known role of Saint’s screen career: Eve Kendell, a steely double agent who gets swept up in a convoluted espionage plot and romance with a dashing Madison Avenue executive (Cary Grant) in “North by Northwest.” Saint was asked to convey equal parts competence and vulnerability, seductiveness and fear. She pulled it off with aplomb. In the film’s deliriously suspenseful climax, Eve tries to fend off villainous operatives atop Mount Rushmore and nearly falls off the mountain. In actuality, she raced around on a 30-foot re-creation of Mount Rushmore inside a Culver City, California, soundstage. Still, the action set piece was not exactly easy to shoot. “I had just given birth two weeks before to our second child,” Saint recalled in a 2000 interview with The Oklahoman. “So, there I was, climbing around. I thought: Oh my, I have no fear of heights, but I don’t climb mountains.” But then she realized she “wasn’t nervous, and Cary was older than I, and I thought: Oh, if he can do it, I can do it,” she told the newspaper. In the years to come, Saint tried her hand at various genres, from the historical epic (Preminger’s “Exodus”) and the domestic melodrama (Minnelli’s “The Sandpiper”) to a memorable Cold War comedy (“The Russians Are Coming! The Russians Are Coming!”). In the 1970s, Saint reduced her feature film commitments and started to appear more frequently in intimate made-for-television films and miniseries, including “The First Woman President” and “Fatal Vision.” In an interview with The Associated Press published in 2014, Saint said she continued to savor the challenge of acting but envied the plum roles handed to veteran British performers such as Judi Dench and Maggie Smith. “We don’t have quite that attitude in Hollywood,” she said. “You reach a certain age and you’re so proud that you’re walking and breathing and loving and working and all of that at 90.” Saint’s last big-screen credit was in the 2014 fantasy romance “Winter’s Tale,” co-starring Colin Farrell and Jessica Brown Findlay, of “Downton Abbey.” Saint recalled that Farrell gave her five dozen roses on the final day of shooting. Saint is survived by her two children, Darrell and Laurette; four grandchildren, Eli, Tyler, Molly and Stella; and two great-grandchildren, Arlo and Finley.

articles.title: ‘Digger’ bombs: A rare box-office misfire for Tom Cruise
articles.summary: Tom Cruise's dark comedy "Digger" earned just $8 million domestically despite a reported budget of up to $150 million, marking a rare career low.
articles.body: You can’t win ’em all. That’s a phrase Hollywood’s global cinematic icon and producer Tom Cruise isn’t likely to hear often. But this past weekend, what many consider Hollywood’s biggest movie star in history suffered one of the worst debuts of his career. The painful performance at the box office of the dark comedy "Digger" was one for the headlines. Cruise earned legendary praise for keeping Paramount’s "Top Gun: Maverick" out of streaming services during the pandemic, forcing a theatrical-only release that grossed $1.5 billion worldwide, and has long been viewed as the studio’s "golden boy," anchoring multibillion-dollar intellectual properties and protecting the traditional theatrical experience. TOM CRUISE UNVEILS DRAMATIC TRANSFORMATION IN FIRST LOOK AT ALEJANDRO IÑÁRRITU’S HIGHLY-ANTICIPATED 'DIGGER' The Alejandro G. Iñárritu-directed "Digger," however, delivered a disappointing farewell note for Warner Bros. as a standalone studio. It grossed only $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally, where Cruise is ordinarily a big draw. That’s despite the film reportedly costing between $125 million and $150 million to make, with marketing expenses estimated at $100 million. "Given his extraordinary history with Paramount, the timing certainly adds an interesting layer to the story, but one movie doesn’t erase decades of success or the value he brings to a studio," Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends for global media measurement and data analytics company Rentrak, told Fox News Digital. "There are lessons to be learned from ‘Digger,’ particularly around budget, positioning and expectations, but I don’t see this changing the fact that studios will continue to want to work with him." Meanwhile, the weekend’s No. 1 box office draw, debuting with $32.6 million, went to Amazon MGM’s erotic psychological thriller "Verity," directed by Michael Showalter and starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett. The film’s strong showing extends a winning streak for adaptations of author Colleen Hoover’s work at the box office. SAUDI-BACKED 'DESERT WARRIOR' GROSSES JUST $472K ON A $150M BUDGET IN HISTORIC BOX OFFICE DISASTER Following "Verity," Zach Cregger’s video game adaptation "Resident Evil" came in second for Sony Pictures with $12.5 million, while Paramount’s "Heart of the Beast," starring Brad Pitt as a former special forces soldier trapped in the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog, grossed $11 million. That was followed by director Lance Oppenheim’s "Primetime" and "Digger." In the case of "Digger," critics weren’t especially kind, with the film earning a 51% score on Rotten Tomatoes. Cruise pulled out all the stops, giving a rare one-on-one interview with GQ magazine as part of the promotional campaign for the climate satire. The film’s London premiere on Sept. 22 at the ODEON Luxe Leicester Square brought out Prince William and Princess Catherine, as the event also served as this year’s royal charity screening benefiting the UK’s Film and TV Charity. While Cruise welcomed the two on the red carpet, David Beckham also made an appearance with his two sons, Cruz and Romeo. TOM CRUISE ADMITS RUMORS ABOUT HIS 'INTENSE' BEHAVIOR ON MOVIE SETS ARE TRUE The underwhelming opening comes as Paramount Skydance closes its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in a $110 billion deal. Despite "Digger’s" poor showing, Dergarabedian said it won’t ultimately affect Cruise as a Hollywood powerhouse. "I think the interesting thing here is that the result really doesn’t change the fundamental reality that every studio wants to be in the Tom Cruise business," he said. "‘Digger’ was always a much tougher commercial proposition than the kind of broad, action-driven, franchise-oriented films audiences traditionally associate with Cruise." articles.title: Iranian director decries Hollywood portrayal of foreign countries, calls American democracy 'a lie'
articles.summary: Director Asghar Farhadi slammed Ben Affleck's "Argo" at the Rio Film Festival, calling it a "Hollywood thing" that portrays Iran "like you're in hell."
articles.body: Oscar-winning Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi called out Hollywood's depiction of Iran and other foreign countries at the Rio Film Festival in Brazil on Friday, claiming it is a "lie" to call America a "democracy." While promoting his film "Parallel Tales," Farhadi was asked about the 2012 movie "Argo" winning Best Picture just one year after his film "A Separation" won Best Foreign Language Film at the Oscars. "Argo," directed by Ben Affleck, stars Affleck as CIA operative Tony Mendez in a loose adaptation of Mendez's memoir on the rescue of six U.S. diplomats from Iran by pretending to film a science-fiction movie in the nation. BEN AFFLECK REJECTS 'PROPAGANDA' OPPOSING AI, INSISTS EMERGING TECHNOLOGY WILL HELP FILMMAKERS Farhadi described the film as a "Hollywood thing" and suggested it was "not deep" based on its plot involving a "White guy" saving others, though Mendez in real life was of Mexican descent. "They make these movies for money; it’s a business," Farhadi said, according to Variety. "And in these films it’s always a [W]hite guy from the United States saving others. My question is: Why? Why does an American go to Cuba or Iran to save people? People understand they can save themselves. Who asked you to come and save us?" Farhadi also accused "Argo," which took place after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, of portraying Iran "like you're in hell." AMERICAN WHO FLED IRAN SAYS CITIZENS 'DESPERATE' FOR FREEDOM, PRAYING FOR ISLAMIC REGIME TO FALL "The problem with these kinds of films in Hollywood [and] some people in the United States [is that] they look at the world from up to down," Farhadi said. "Someday you should ask them: Why do you feel you’re up and we’re down? I don’t understand why they have this ego that they’re up." Farhadi also denied Americans' claim to "have democracy," saying he believed the "real America" exists among Black and foreign prisoners. "You don’t have democracy. It’s a lie," Farhadi said. VICTOR DAVIS HANSON DISSECTS HOW CRITICS COMPLETELY MISREAD THE IRAN DEAL Fox News Digital reached out to Farhadi's and Affleck's representatives for comment. Media Research Center President David Bozell called out Farhadi's negative view of America and American films in a comment to Fox News Digital. articles.title: Eva Marie Saint, Oscar-winning ‘On the Waterfront’ and ‘North by Northwest’ star, dead at 102
articles.summary: Oscar winning actress Eva Marie Saint, who starred opposite Marlon Brando and Cary Grant, has died at 102 after a career spanning seven decades.
articles.body: Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar-and Emmy-winning actress who became one of the defining stars of Hollywood’s Golden Era, has died. She was 102. Saint died Tuesday of natural causes at her Los Angeles home surrounded by family and loved ones, her representative confirmed to Fox News Digital. The actress made an extraordinary film debut opposite Marlon Brando in the 1954 classic "On the Waterfront," winning the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress in her performance as Edie Doyle. Directed by Elia Kazan, the landmark drama launched Saint onto the big screen after she had already established herself in television and on the New York stage. Her first movie role placed her opposite Brando at the apex of his fame. POST MALONE, EVA MARIE SAINT AND OTHER CELEBRITIES WHO SHARE A BIRTHDAY WITH THE FOURTH OF JULY Five years later, Saint then firmly cemented her place in Hollywood's Golden Era history while starring opposite the legendary Cary Grant in Alfred Hitchcock’s "North by Northwest," playing mysterious "Hitchcock Blonde" Eve Kendall in the cult-classic 1959 thriller. The role offered a striking contrast to the vulnerable, angelic young woman she portrayed in "On the Waterfront." As Hitchcock’s elegant and enigmatic leading lady, Saint became part of one of the British director’s most enduring films, sharing the screen with Grant in a movie remembered for its sweeping romance, suspense and iconic Mount Rushmore climax. Saint’s two best-known films alone paired her with Brando, Kazan, Grant and Hitchcock, but represent only the start of a career that would stretch more than 70 years. Over an incredible career spanning more than seven decades, Saint worked alongside some of Hollywood’s most celebrated leading men, including Montgomery Clift, Henry Fonda, Paul Newman, Gregory Peck, Richard Burton, Warren Beatty, James Garner, George C. Scott, Burt Lancaster and Tom Hanks. OSCAR-WINNER BRENDA FRICKER, 'PIGEON LADY' FROM 'HOME ALONE 2,' DEAD AT 81 Her list of co-stars reads like a roll call of midcentury Hollywood. She appeared with Clift and Elizabeth Taylor in "Raintree County," Newman in "Exodus," Beatty in "All Fall Down," Burton in "The Sandpiper" and Garner in the racing epic "Grand Prix." Other notable films featuring the actress included "A Hatful of Rain," "Raintree County," "Exodus," "The Russians Are Coming the Russians Are Coming," "Grand Prix," "Nothing in Common" and, later in her career, "Superman Returns." Saint was also a regular fixture of television and the stage. She earned five Emmy nominations, winning in 1990 for the miniseries "People Like Us," and appeared on Broadway in "The Trip to Bountiful" before director Elia Kazan cast her in "On the Waterfront." SHELLEY FABARES, STAR OF 'THE DONNA REED SHOW' AND 'COACH,' DEAD AT 82 Her career had actually begun during the golden age of live television. Saint earned early Emmy nominations for Paddy Chayefsky’s "Middle of the Night" and a live television musical adaptation of Thornton Wilder’s "Our Town," in which she played Emily alongside Frank Sinatra and Paul Newman. On Broadway, her performance in the Christian-themed "The Trip to Bountiful" earned her critical acclaim and caught Kazan’s attention. Saint's moves from radio and live television to Broadway and then an Oscar-winning movie debut uniquely placed her at the crossroads of several defining eras of 20th century American entertainment. Born in Newark, New Jersey, and raised in Albany and Delmar, New York, Saint attended Bowling Green State University in Ohio with plans to become a teacher before acting ultimately changed the course of her life. She tried out for a university play at the suggestion of a drama professor, won the leading role and abandoned her original plan to become a schoolteacher. After graduation, she moved to New York City, studying at the American Theatre Wing and with Lee Strasberg at the Actors Studio. Bowling Green later awarded Saint an honorary Doctor of Fine Arts degree and renamed its main campus theater the Eva Marie Saint Theatre. She returned to the Academy Awards as a presenter in 2009 and again in 2018, receiving a standing ovation from the stars gathered when she walked onto the stage at age 93. PAUL ANKA SLAMS MODERN SINGERS, SAYS FRANK SINATRA WOULD HAVE 'THROWN A CHAIR' Saint was married to director Jeffrey Hayden for 65 years until his death in 2016. She is survived by their two children, Darrell and Laurette, four grandchildren, Eli, Tyler, Molly and Stella, and two great-grandchildren, Arlo and Finley. From the docks of "On the Waterfront" to the intrigue and glamour of "North by Northwest," Saint became an undisputed face of Hollywood history while building a body of work that endured long after that era had passed. articles.body: Eva Marie Saint, one of the silver screen's most graceful stars, has passed away. She left for her heavenly abode at 102. The Oscar-winning actress, Marie, was well known for her work in films like ‘On the Waterfront,' 'Exodus,' ‘Nothing in Common,' and 'Superman Returns,' to name a few.Veteran actress Eva Marie Saint passes away at 102Deadline reported that the beloved actress passed away at her Los Angeles home on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at the age of 102. Loved ones surrounded her and her family members at the time. The report cited natural causes for her demise.Who was Eva Marie Saint?Eva Marie Saint was born on July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey. Working with the likes of Marlon Brando, Cary Grant, and Alfred Hitchcock, the actress was one of the most well-known and sought-after faces in the Hollywood industry at the time. She mainly grew up in Albany and Delmar, New York. As for her education, Saint studied acting at Bowling Green State University in Ohio. She graduated in 1946 and took up jobs in New York City as an NBC page, all the while studying at the American Theatre Wing and with Lee Strasberg at The Actors Studio.Eva Marie won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her feature film debut as Edie Doyle in Elia Kazan’s 1954 classic On the Waterfront, starring opposite Marlon Brando. Alfred Hitchcock’s film launched her into stardom, which she was extremely grateful for. While talking to Vanity Fair in 2014 about working on the film, she revealed that Hitchcock even let her choose the clothes for her role.She added, “He didn’t talk about acting. He worked with me from the outside in. My hair, my makeup, my shoes, my jewellery, my purse, my gloves, everything. And just from creating that exterior for me, he gave me the sense of a spy lady. But we never talked about emotion. He told me not to use my hands; I have a habit of doing that, and to lower my voice. And always, in my scenes with Cary Grant, look directly into his eyes, which was not difficult.”After her big launch into the world of stardom, Eva appeared in a lot of films and TV shows over the course of her career. She went on to co-star in major productions like Otto Preminger's ‘Exodus’ (1960) with Paul Newman, John Frankenheimer's ‘Grand Prix' (1966), and ‘The Russians Are Coming, the Russians Are Coming’ (1966). She also dabbled in TV and played recurring television roles, such as Cybill Shepherd's mother in ‘Moonlighting’ in the 1980s, and she also won an Emmy Award for the miniseries ‘People Like Us’ (1990) and appeared as Martha Kent in ‘Superman Returns’ (2006)Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Oscar-winning On the Waterfront actress Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102
articles.summary: She starred opposite Marlon Brando in On the Waterfront, then alongside Cary Grant in Hitchcock's North by Northwest.
articles.body:
Eva Marie Saint, the Oscar-winning actress who starred in Hollywood classics such as On the Waterfront and North by Northwest, has died aged 102.

Saint won the Academy Award for best supporting actress for her movie debut in director Elia Kazan's 1954 crime thriller On the Waterfront, playing Edie Doyle, the love interest of Marlon Brando's conflicted ex-boxing docker.

Five years later, she portrayed femme fatale Eve Kendall, dangerously seducing Cary Grant in Alfred Hitchcock's action thriller North by Northwest.

She died on Tuesday of natural causes, surrounded by family and loved ones at her home in Los Angeles, family representative Jeff Sanderson confirmed.

Until her death, Saint was the oldest surviving Oscar winner and one of the last remaining stars of Hollywood's golden age.

She also won an Emmy in 1990 for her role as a rich widow in the acclaimed TV miniseries People Like Us.

Born in Newark, New Jersey, Saint had originally intended to become a teacher before developing a passion for theatre.

She trained in New York at the Herbert Berghof Studio and then the Actors Studio - the home of method acting - co-founded by Kazan.

Saint burst on to the Hollywood scene with her performance in Kazan's classic, On the Waterfront.

Brando was known as an intense method actor and Saint admitted to having found him "adorable" but "a little frightening".

"I felt that he could see right through me," she told Turner Classic Movies (TCM) in a 2013 interview.

She was considered a surprise choice, though, to play one of "Hitchcock's blondes", as they were known at the time, in his masterpiece North by Northwest.

Her co-star Grant was known for being very demanding of his leading ladies.

"He worked with me from the outside in," said Saint.

"My hair, my makeup, my shoes, my jewellery, my purse, my gloves, everything. And just from creating that exterior for me, he gave me the sense of a spy lady."

Saint also starred opposite Paul Newman in Otto Preminger's Exodus in 1960, and she was Warren Beatty's love interest in John Frankenheimer's All Fall Down.

But she then stepped away from the limelight to raise a family with director Jeffrey Hayden.

Half a century later, Saint - by then in her early 80s - made a big screen comeback as Superman's adoptive mother in the 2006 blockbuster Superman Returns.

And she later had parts in the supernatural fantasy Winter's Tale, alongside Colin Farrell and Russell Crowe, and another in the 2019 nun drama Mariette in Ecstasy.

Saint, who has two stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, said her longevity in acting had given her work extra depth.

"The longer you live, the smarter you get, because you've been around, you've seen things," she told TCM.

"You've gone through different emotional experiences in your own life, and hopefully, you understand things better.

Saint's marriage to Hayden lasted for 65 years, until his death in 2016, and she is survived by their two children.

articles.title: Virat Kohli denies claim that him and Anushka Sharma were being paid Rs 5 crore for visiting Premanand ji Maharaj: 'Purely out of his deep faith and reverence'

articles.body: The death of a disciple of Premanand ji Maharaj has brought renewed attention to his Vrindavan ashram, with allegations being made about the way the establishment was allegedly promoted and used by certain groups. Among the claims that surfaced was one involving cricketer Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma and their visit to Premanand ji Maharaj. The allegation was made by Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma, president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas. Following the death of Premanand Maharaj’s disciple Rasik Dulari under mysterious circumstances at the Radha Keli Kunj Ashram, Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Kohli’s first visit to the ashram.With the allegation now being widely discussed, Kohli’s team has issued a clarification, firmly denying that he was paid to visit the spiritual leader. The official statement said, “We would like to categorically state that the claims made by Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma in regards to Mr Virat Kohli are completely false, baseless and factually incorrect.”The statement also made it clear that Kohli’s visits were motivated by his personal faith rather than any financial arrangement. “Mr Virat Kohli visits Premanand Maharaj Ji purely out of his deep faith and reverence for Maharaj Ji,” it read.Kohli’s team further urged media organisations and others sharing the allegation to verify the claims before amplifying them. “We strongly refute these claims and urge the media to exercise due diligence, verify facts before reporting or amplifying such statements, and report responsibly.”For those not in the know, Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma made the allegation in a letter addressed to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. He claimed that the money was allegedly spent to bring Kohli to the ashram in a bid to increase its popularity and reach. He also alleged that a builder lobby and land mafia had been using the name of Premanand Maharaj’s ashram for public relations and an alleged extortion racket. These allegations have not been established, and the investigation into Rasik Dulari’s death is underway.Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma first visited Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan on January 4, 2023, to seek his blessings. Their association with the spiritual leader continued after that, with the couple making several visits over the years, including around IPL matches and during their trips to India from London.Their visits have repeatedly attracted attention on the internet, with videos from the ashram often going viral. The couple’s most recent visit was on July 22, 2026, when they were seen walking barefoot through the drizzle at the Vrindavan ashram to seek Premanand Maharaj’s blessings.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' continues its theatrical run with the Ajay Devgn-led franchise finale maintaining a strong hold at the domestic box office. After crossing Rs. 200 crore India net in just five days since its release over the Gandhi Jayanti weekend, the film has now entered Day 6 of its theatrical run, closing in on the Rs. 220 crore domestic net mark and inching towards the coveted Rs 250 crore milestone.On the worldwide front, the film has already moved beyond Rs. 340 crore and could next look towards Rs 350 crore mark, before setting its sights on the Rs 400 crore milestone if its theatrical momentum remains strong, subject to robust reviews translating into footfalls. The second weekend will be particularly important in determining how quickly the film can approach these milestones.'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion' domestic box office runThe film opened with a Rs. 62 crore net on Day 1 and added Rs. 53.50 crore on Day 2. Day 3 brought a jump to Rs. 61 crore, helped by the weekend. The first Monday saw a natural depression with the film's collection dropping to Rs. 21 crore on Day 4 and Day 5 followed it up with Rs. 19.50 crore. That took the India net to Rs. 217 crore and the India gross to Rs. 260.40 crore by the end of Day 5.‘Drishyam 3 The Conclusion’ overseas collection and worldwide totalOverseas, the film made Rs. 18.50 crore on Day 1 and Rs. 20 crore each on Day 2 and Day 3. The overseas gross is reported at Rs. 81.50 crore, which put the worldwide total at Rs. 341.90 crore.'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion' Day 6 collection live trackingAccording to Sacnilk, 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' has added Rs. 2.32 crore net to its India tally so far.The film is currently running across 5,932 shows, pushing its total domestic net collection to Rs. 219.32 crore and India gross to Rs. 263.14 crore, with final figures tallied and updated at the end of the day.Day wise collections for 'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion'Day 1: Rs. 62.00 croreDay 2: Rs. 53.50 croreDay 3: Rs. 61.00 croreDay 4: Rs. 21.00 croreDay 5: Rs. 19.50 croreDay 6 [LIVE]: Rs. 2.32 croreTOTAL: Rs. 219.32 croreMore about 'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion''Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' brings the protagonist Vijay Salgaonkar's story to its final chapter. Following up on its predecessor, 'Drishyam' (2015) and 'Drishyam 2' (2022), the third instalment continues the central conflict, starring Ajay Devgn as the cable-operator-turned-cinema-buff Vijay Salgaonkar. The narrative chronicles around a middle-class father using his extensive knowledge of movie tropes and human psychology to protect his family from the law after an accidental murder.Apart from Devgn, the ensemble cast features Shriya Saran reprising her role as Nandini and Ishita Dutta returns as Anju. Tabu is back as Meera Deshmukh. The cast also features Prakash Raj and Jaideep Ahlawat in new roles, alongside Rajat Kapoor, Saurabh Shukla and Kamlesh Sawant. articles.title: Nicole Kidman, Zendaya and hovering cars see Paris Fashion Week go out on a high
articles.summary: Nicole Kidman, Zendaya and hovering cars see Paris Fashion Week go out on a high.
articles.body: PARIS — Coco Chanel designed her postwar suit so women could move. Seven decades later, designer Matthieu Blazy has made it stretch. Suits in a new “smocked tweed” anchored Blazy’s spring-summer 2027 collection for Chanel, shown Monday night at the Grand Palais beneath a flock of illuminated birds as Nicole Kidman, Dua Lipa and Pedro Pascal watched from the front row. The fabric gives like sportswear, but the idea is old. Chanel built its name by changing how women dressed, and a year after his debut as its designer, Blazy is applying that principle to the house’s own uniform. Louis Vuitton closed Paris Fashion Week on Tuesday evening with Zendaya in the audience and car sculptures hovering above the runway at the Louvre Museum. It was the final major show of a spring runway season that began in New York last month. Blazy came from Bottega Veneta to succeed the longtime right hand of Karl Lagerfeld, Virginie Viard, who took over after Lagerfeld’s death in 2019. Viard’s tenure brought record sales. Blazy’s has brought back surprise. He loosens the house’s symbols rather than replacing them. Tweed stretches. Jackets go on over bare skin. Quilted bags slouch. Longtime clients still recognize the codes; newer ones are invited to play with them. This season, he staged Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel’s life as an escape: from the corsets and stiff tailoring of her Edwardian youth, through the men’s clothes she borrowed, to the easy suits of her postwar comeback. “It’s about the women within a woman,” Blazy said. Kidman, who attended with her daughter Faith Margaret, also supplied recorded readings from Virginia Woolf’s “Orlando,” whose protagonist lives across centuries and changes sex. Kidman won an Oscar for portraying Woolf in “The Hours.” Kidman, Lipa, Pascal and Alexa Demie sang along to a-ha’s “Take On Me,” and the show ended with Britney Spears’ “Gimme More.” On the Chanel runway Edwardian dress lingered in traces of boning, peplums and ruffled collars. Men’s formal wear was cut down into raw-edged vests and narrow skirt suits. A pearl-stitched corset top worn with plain black trousers complicated the story of escape, making constraint part of the appeal. The most beautiful pieces were dresses of layered, printed silk that tracked the sky from morning to nightfall, and 1930s-style sequined or beaded gowns that Chanel described as having the ease of a T-shirt. Not everything landed. Pattern-on-pattern outfits and ballet tutus tipped into costume, and at 83 looks, the argument sometimes sprawled. The birds made it more gracefully: swallows perched on buttons and jewelry, and a birdcage evening bag came with its birds already flown. Model Dyanira Hurbuscher walked first and last, both times carrying the founder’s own 2.55 handbag from the house archives — freedom, with the past firmly in hand. Vuitton lightens up Louis Vuitton offered a softer vision of the future — and another argument for giving the body room to move. Nicolas Ghesquière, known for sculpted, futuristic silhouettes, loosened things up with gauzy shift dresses, cardigans, short jackets and soft tailoring. Delicate fabrics rippled as models walked, and slim trousers incorporated sheer mesh panels. His taste for science fiction remained intact. An asphalt runway crossed the Louvre’s Cour Carrée beneath dozens of wedge-shaped concept cars raised on poles and decorated in the house’s Damier checkerboard pattern. Silver lamé gave some shift dresses a metallic flash. Zendaya, a house ambassador, brought some informality to the front row, pairing jeans with the ruffled white lace jacket that she had worn to the Paris premiere of “The Odyssey.” Emma Stone, Saoirse Ronan, Blackpink’s Lisa, Sophie Turner and Catherine Deneuve also attended. Paris loosens up Across Paris, designers made similar moves: mixing formal clothes with sportswear, bringing lingerie into public view and making elaborate decoration feel lighter. Miu Miu worked the same seam from the opposite side, dressing sportswear up. Miuccia Prada paired pleated check skirts and blazers with running shorts and track tops. Shoelaces became belts, and guests watched from gym-style bleachers. Olivia Colman modeled a black leather skirt suit, joining Jamie Bell and Emma Corrin on the runway. Sacai’s Chitose Abe, back on the women’s runway after a season away, set tough clothes in motion. Biker leathers broke into swinging fringe, silk tassels crowned military jackets, and prints of beads and rhinestones under sheer layers gave the look of embellishment without the weight. She finished by running to hug Pharrell Williams. At Valentino, plain satin bustiers and knee-length skirts offered a more intimate kind of formality. Showing at the Sainte-Geneviève Library, Alessandro Michele compared unworn clothes with unread books in his notes: both “still speak to us of the lives we could have lived.” Alexander Skarsgård brought Icelandic sagas to donate. Elie Saab took lingerie in a more nostalgic direction. Beaded slips and lace bralettes recalled the early 2000s, when Halle Berry won her Oscar in one of his gowns. Paris and Nicky Hilton sat in the front row. Victoria Beckham’s pleated dresses hung from jewelry chains, taffeta raincoats looked weightless and wedge sandals had their heels hollowed out. As with Blazy’s stretch tweed, the ambition was to make elaborate clothes feel easy to wear.

articles.title: Advocates decry detention of Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh by ICE in US
articles.summary: Arfat Sheikh was arrested at Washington Dulles International Airport on September 24, advocacy group says.
articles.body:
Supporters of Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh have called for his immediate release after he was arrested by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents last month.

“Sheikh was unlawfully detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement at Washington Dulles International Airport on September 24, 2026,” the Free Arfat Sheikh campaign, an advocacy group, said in a statement on Tuesday.

The 42-year-old artist, who resides in Alexandria, Virginia, arrived in the US on a student visa in 2019 to pursue graduate studies in film at Georgia State University and sought asylum in 2020, the campaign said.

Sheikh is being held in the Caroline Detention Facility in Bowling Green, Virginia, it added.

The filmmaker was scheduled to appear before an immigration judge on Tuesday for a procedural hearing alongside a bond assessment, the press release said.

There has been no comment regarding the detention from ICE or the Department of Homeland Security.

Sheikh’s first feature film Saffron Kingdom garnered multiple honours, notably Best Feature Film at the Chicago Filmmakers Awards, LA Film and Documentary Awards, Melbourne Independent Film Festival, Wake Forest Film Festival, and Anatolian International Film Awards, the advocacy campaign noted.

In 2025, Sheikh was also recognised with the Emerging Filmmaker Activist Award at the Teaneck International Film Festival.

Sheikh’s detention comes as the number of ICE arrests across the US hit record levels this summer, with about 50,000 arrests recorded in July and August.
